### Model stg_payments
File: models/staging/stg_payments.sql · materialized as view
Description: Cleaned payments, one row per payment. Amount converted from cents to currency units.
Columns (name · type in warehouse · description · tests):
- payment_id · INTEGER · Primary key of the payment. · tests: unique, not_null
- order_id · INTEGER · Order the payment belongs to (foreign key to stg_orders). · tests: not_null, relationships(to=stg_orders, field=order_id)
- payment_method · VARCHAR · Payment method used. · tests: accepted_values(values=['credit_card', 'bank_transfer', 'voucher', 'gift_card'])
- amount · DOUBLE · Payment amount in currency units (raw cents / 100). · tests: not_null
- loaded_at · TIMESTAMP · UTC timestamp when the row was loaded into the warehouse.
SQL (models/staging/stg_payments.sql):
```sql
with source as (

    select * from {{ source('raw', 'raw_payments') }}

),

renamed as (

    select
        payment_id,
        order_id,
        payment_method,
        -- source stores integer cents; convert to currency units
        cast(amount as decimal(18, 2)) / 100 as amount,
        loaded_at
    from source

)

select * from renamed
```

### Model stg_orders
File: models/staging/stg_orders.sql · materialized as view
Description: Cleaned orders, one row per order. Expected volume is 500-1,000 orders over the 180-day window.
Columns (name · type in warehouse · description · tests):
- order_id · INTEGER · Primary key of the order. · tests: unique, not_null
- customer_id · INTEGER · Customer who placed the order (foreign key to stg_customers). · tests: not_null
- order_date · DATE · Date the order was placed. · tests: not_null
- status · VARCHAR · Order lifecycle status. · tests: accepted_values(values=['placed', 'shipped', 'completed', 'cancelled'])
- loaded_at · TIMESTAMP · UTC timestamp when the row was loaded into the warehouse.
Model-level tests: row_count_between(min_rows=500, max_rows=1000)
SQL (models/staging/stg_orders.sql):
```sql
with source as (

    select * from {{ source('raw', 'raw_orders') }}

),

renamed as (

    select
        order_id,
        customer_id,
        cast(order_date as date) as order_date,
        status,
        loaded_at
    from source

)

select * from renamed
```

gold_standard_remediation.root_cause: The 6 payments that fail the relationships test on stg_payments.order_id all belong to orders 12, 22, 36, 179, 264. Those orders, and customer 3, were deleted from the shop and CRM data under erasure request DPR-1093. The payment data was not included in the erasure, so raw.raw_payments still holds those payments. This is not late-arriving data: the orders will never arrive.
gold_standard_remediation.fix: Complete the erasure: ask the data-protection owner and the payment provider to delete or anonymise those payments, as the retention policy allows. Meanwhile, keep the orphan payments out of the models explicitly: add a seed `erased_orders` (order_id) and exclude its order_ids in models/staging/stg_payments.sql (`where order_id not in (select order_id from {{ ref('erased_orders') }})`), so the exclusion is auditable. Don't relax the relationships test.
gold_standard_remediation.verification: `dbt build --select stg_payments+` passes. `select count(*) from stg_payments where order_id in (12, 22, 36, 179, 264)` returns 0.
gold_standard_remediation.text:
Root cause: The 6 payments that fail the relationships test on stg_payments.order_id all belong to orders 12, 22, 36, 179, 264. Those orders, and customer 3, were deleted from the shop and CRM data under erasure request DPR-1093. The payment data was not included in the erasure, so raw.raw_payments still holds those payments. This is not late-arriving data: the orders will never arrive.

Fix: Complete the erasure: ask the data-protection owner and the payment provider to delete or anonymise those payments, as the retention policy allows. Meanwhile, keep the orphan payments out of the models explicitly: add a seed `erased_orders` (order_id) and exclude its order_ids in models/staging/stg_payments.sql (`where order_id not in (select order_id from {{ ref('erased_orders') }})`), so the exclusion is auditable. Don't relax the relationships test.

Verification: `dbt build --select stg_payments+` passes. `select count(*) from stg_payments where order_id in (12, 22, 36, 179, 264)` returns 0.
